title: Flip scroll path: one element carried through the page's own slots
summary: One CSS-drawn picture flown through four empty slots that the grid, `aspect-ratio` and `border-radius` lay out (an arch, a square, a 21:9 shelf, a circle) by `Flip.fit(flyer, nextSlot, { simple: true, scale: false })` legs chained into one `scrub: .6` timeline whose unit is the scroll pixel: slot k is fitted where its centre meets the viewport's, each leg lasts its scroll distance minus a dwell of `.3` viewport in which the picture rides with its slot, and a linear `borderRadius` tween to the slot's own corner runs beside each leg; the timeline is torn down on `refreshInit` and rebuilt on `refresh`, and a height change of `main` asks for a refresh, so resize, load and text zoom re-measure; the flyer is `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none` and `contain: strict`, the picture is drawn in container units so it art-directs itself to each box; reduced motion and static show each slot's own still and fly nothing
variants: one element through four slots in four sections, dwell in each, rebuilt on refresh (this, default)
no dwell: legs from centre to centre, so the element floats at the viewport's middle and only touches each slot
scale: true legs for a picture whose slots share one aspect ratio (transform only, no width or height writes)
